steps.narration: VentiLab turns a classroom into a clean-air physics laboratory. Everything runs offline in the browser, with no data leaving the device.
Switching to cross ventilation opens two opposing window paths. Wind and the indoor-outdoor temperature difference combine by root-sum-square.
The window opening slider controls how much outdoor air reaches the room. Carbon dioxide falls as the opening grows.
On a wildfire day the trade-off reverses. Outdoor fine particles reach one hundred eighty micrograms per cubic meter.
A Corsi-Rosenthal fan box and a portable HEPA unit add clean-air delivery, shown as a separate equivalent airflow.
Filtration cleans particles but does not remove exhaled carbon dioxide, so both models must be read together.
Masks reduce emission; ventilation, filtration and upper-room UVGI speed removal.
Each point trades cost against remaining risk, power, noise, carbon dioxide and particles. No point on the frontier is dominated.
The table view exposes every simulated value, because identity is never carried by color alone.
Carbon-dioxide root-mean-square error is about eight times ten to the minus nine percent, far below the point-zero-five-percent target.
The printable action card carries results back to class. VentiLab makes the invisible visible, and gives students an honest way to argue with numbers.
